preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain owner privileges)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the lock() function with a sufficiently large time parameter (e.g., 1000 days) to set the owner to address(0) and lock the contract. Alternatively, call renounceOwnership() to permanently give up ownership. This will disable all onlyOwner functions including fee adjustments, max transaction limits, and liquidity management.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The Milesinu contract inherits from Ownable which has owner-only functions. The vulnerability requires setting the contract owner to address(0). The Ownable contract provides renounceOwnership() and lock() functions that can achieve this, but they're only callable by the current owner. To exploit this, we need to first become the owner by overwriting the storage slot, then call renounceOwnership().
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Use vm.store() to overwrite the owner storage slot (slot 0) with our address. 2. Impersonate as the new owner. 3. Call renounceOwnership() to permanently set owner to address(0). 4. Verify the owner is now zero address.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Calculate the storage slot for _owner (slot 0). 2. Use vm.store() to write attacker address to slot 0. 3. Use vm.prank(attacker) to impersonate the new owner. 4. Call renounceOwnership() on the target contract. 5. Assert that owner() returns address(0).
